options.A: every debit entry has a corresponding credit entry
options.B: every transaction is recorded twice in the same account

explanationCorrect: Each transaction affects two accounts: one debited and one credited with the same amount.

explanationsWrong.B: The two entries go into two different accounts.

stem: A business has assets of ₦50,000 and liabilities of ₦20,000. What is its capital?

explanationsWrong.C: Capital is found by subtraction, not division.

topicName: Source documents and books of original entry
stem: Goods bought on credit from Ade are recorded by
explanationCorrect: Purchases (the goods coming in) is debited; Ade (the creditor giving value) is credited.

explanationsWrong.B: No cash is involved in a credit purchase.
explanationsWrong.D: Crediting cash would mean paying immediately.

stem: The main purpose of a trial balance is to

options.B: check the arithmetical accuracy of the ledger

explanationCorrect: If total debits equal total credits, the double entry is arithmetically correct (though some errors stay hidden).

explanationsWrong.A: Profit is calculated in the trading and profit and loss account.
explanationsWrong.C: The balance sheet shows financial position.

topicName: Correction of errors and suspense account
stem: Which error is NOT revealed by a trial balance?

options.C: Wrong addition of one side of an account
options.D: Entering a debit as ₦500 and the credit as ₦50

explanationCorrect: If a transaction is left out completely, both debit and credit are missing, so the trial balance still agrees.

explanationsWrong.B: A single entry makes the totals unequal.
explanationsWrong.C: A casting error on one side makes the totals unequal.
explanationsWrong.D: Unequal amounts make the totals disagree.

stem: Cheques issued by a business but not yet presented to the bank are called
explanationCorrect: They are in the cash book but not yet on the bank statement, so they appear in the reconciliation.

explanationsWrong.A: Dishonoured cheques are refused by the bank.
explanationsWrong.B: Uncredited cheques (lodgements) are deposits not yet on the statement.
explanationsWrong.C: Crossing is a way of making cheques safer.

stem: Under the imprest system of petty cash, the petty cashier is

options.A: given a new amount each day
options.C: given a fixed float and reimbursed for what is spent

explanationCorrect: The float is restored to the same amount at the end of each period by reimbursing actual spending.

explanationsWrong.A: The float is fixed, not a new amount daily.
explanationsWrong.B: Unspent cash stays as part of the float.

topicName: Final accounts of a sole trader
stem: Opening stock ₦5,000; purchases ₦20,000; closing stock ₦3,000; sales ₦30,000. What is the gross profit?

explanationsWrong.C: ₦2,000 takes both stock figures off sales; closing stock reduces cost of sales instead.

stem: A machine costs ₦10,000, has a residual value of ₦2,000 and a useful life of 4 years. Annual straight-line depreciation is
An asset costing ₦10,000 is depreciated at 10% per year on the reducing balance method. What is the depreciation in year 2?

explanationsWrong.C: ₦2,000 is two years at the year-1 amount.

stem: Under FIFO stock valuation, closing stock is valued at
explanationCorrect: First in, first out: the oldest stock is sold first, so what remains is valued at the latest prices.

explanationsWrong.A: Earliest prices are assigned to goods sold under FIFO.
explanationsWrong.B: That is the weighted average method.
explanationsWrong.D: Stock is valued at cost (or net realisable value), not selling price.

stem: The sales ledger control account is used to check the accuracy of
explanationCorrect: It summarises all debtors' (customers') accounts so totals can be checked.

explanationsWrong.A: Creditors are checked by the purchases ledger control account.
explanationsWrong.C: The cash book is checked by a bank reconciliation.
explanationsWrong.D: Fixed assets aren't checked by a control account.

stem: Where proper books are not kept, capital at a date is found by preparing a
explanationCorrect: A statement of affairs lists assets and liabilities; capital = assets − liabilities.

explanationsWrong.B: A trial balance needs complete double-entry records.
explanationsWrong.C: A cash flow statement shows cash movements.
explanationsWrong.D: A bank reconciliation matches the cash book to the bank statement.

stem: Prime cost is the total of

options.D: direct materials, direct labour and direct expenses

explanationCorrect: Prime cost = direct materials + direct labour + direct expenses.

explanationsWrong.A: Factory overheads are added after prime cost.
explanationsWrong.B: All production costs = prime cost + factory overheads (production cost).

stem: In a club's income and expenditure account, an excess of income over expenditure is called a
explanationCorrect: Non-profit organisations call it a surplus (and a deficit if expenditure is higher).

explanationsWrong.D: 'Balance' is used in the receipts and payments account.

stem: In the absence of a partnership agreement, profits are shared
explanationCorrect: Under the Partnership Act 1890, profits and losses are shared equally when there's no agreement.

explanationsWrong.A: Capital ratio applies only if agreed.
explanationsWrong.C: Hours worked isn't the legal default.
explanationsWrong.D: No partner decides alone by law.

stem: Current assets are ₦40,000 and current liabilities are ₦20,000. The current ratio is
explanationCorrect: Current ratio = current assets ÷ current liabilities = 40,000 ÷ 20,000 = 2 : 1.

explanationsWrong.C: ₦20,000 is working capital (CA − CL), not the ratio.

stem: In Nigeria, the main fund into which most federal government revenue is paid is the
explanationCorrect: The Constitution requires federal revenues to be paid into the Consolidated Revenue Fund.

explanationsWrong.A: The Contingencies Fund is for urgent unforeseen spending.
explanationsWrong.B: Development funds hold capital expenditure, not most revenue.
